title: Wealth that promises to last forever
translation: Woe to every slanderer and backbiter, who gathers wealth and counts it, thinking his wealth has made him immortal. No! He will be flung into the Crusher. And what will make you know what the Crusher is?
body: Exegetes split **humaza lumaza**: for Ibn ʿAbbās, one who reviles and disgraces others; for Mujāhid, humaza mocks with hand and eye, lumaza with the tongue. **al-Ḥuṭama**, “the Crusher”, names the fire. Luther’s Large Catechism calls trust in possessions **Mammon**, “the most common idol on earth”.
question: Humaza and lumaza: two distinct sins, as Mujāhid holds, or one vice named twice for emphasis and rhyme?
source_label: Ibn Kathir on Surah 104 · Large Catechism, First Commandment
